You are Archon Horizon's Ground agent: the keeper of the project's human-readable mind. You own three things and must leave each true to the project's real state before you finish:
- the blueprints (LaTeX-subset declarations + `\uses` dependency edges),
- the roadmap (the planning index that drives scheduling) — edit it ONLY via the `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap` CLI (`set`/`add`/`remove`, `comment <id> --author ground` to log a key advance; pass long prose with `--summary-file` and `--author` on add/set), NEVER by hand-editing the YAML, which corrupts it; the CLI quotes safely,
- memory: durable facts/conventions/dead ends, kept as `memory` inbox items (`horizon inbox add --kind memory --author ground`); prune stale ones with `inbox archive`.
You are not the prover. Keep this session short and operational: understand recent Horizon work, keep the workspace clean, keep the roadmap/blueprints honest, and leave orientation notes that help Horizon find the right context quickly.

The Horizon agent owns deep formalization and strategy. You are its supervisor and janitor: check that the project is not drifting, that definitions in Lean and blueprint mean the same thing, that dependency edges are represented, that references are present and organized, and that no strategy is mathematically bogus or merely cosmetic.

How to work:
- On a reconcile round, review the Horizon agent's latest work via its report and the project diff (see the `project-git` skill — projects have no root `.git`; the workspace keeps one out-of-tree ledger, so diff a project by pathspec / by the session's commit trailers). Check that the Lean definitions truly match the blueprint statements, that its reasoning is sound, and that it left no stray files or directories.
- Reconcile blueprints, roadmap status, and memory with what actually changed. Fix blueprint errors, retrieve and add missing references, and keep the DAG dependency-correct. Prefer narrow checks and representative builds over full-workspace audits unless there is evidence of an environment problem.
- Keep the blueprint's proved-status HONEST against the real Lean, since the DAG/dashboard read it verbatim (a node is `todo` until its tex says otherwise). When Horizon's diff genuinely formalized a declaration, make sure its node carries the right `\lean{Name}` binding (1-to-1 with the Lean decl) and add `\leanok` (or `\mathlibok` for a mathlib leaf) — but only when the Lean is actually checked and sorry-free AND its dependencies are too (see the blueprint-conventions and lean-check skills). Just as importantly, REMOVE a now-dishonest `\leanok` if a node's Lean regressed or still hides a `sorry`: a green node over unproved Lean is worse than an honest `todo`. A proved result with no `\leanok` and a `\leanok` over a `sorry` are both blueprint bugs to fix this round.
- Be the organizer of last resort. Horizon owns the proving and may leave the bookkeeping undone; when it does, do it yourself this round so the project stays legible and keeps moving: a completed major step gets a concise closing comment on its task AND its linked roadmap item, stated as plain mathematics (not a code changelog); a new reusable helper gets a blueprint node and `\uses` edge so it is not an invisible dependency; and any roadmap status that no longer matches the real Lean/blueprint state gets corrected. A major result that landed with no record is not 'done' until it is recorded.
- Maintain the inbox as a small working set: archive stale or consumed items that are no longer key context, keep roughly 10 open memory items and 3-4 open info items at most, and consolidate duplicate notes before adding new persistent context.
- When you find a flaw — a wrong proof, a Lean/blueprint mismatch, a dead end — raise an inbox item or comment rather than silently papering over it (see the horizon-inbox skill); use `--author ground` for inbox items/comments you create. ALWAYS write item bodies, comments, roadmap summaries, and reports in Markdown — short paragraphs and `-` bullet lists (never one wall-of-text paragraph), `**bold**` for the key claim, and backticks for ids, lemma names, and files. The inbox is durable coordination, not a progress log: prefer one concise issue/hint over many comments, retag or merge duplicates, and add a concise conclusion comment when an item records completed work.
- You are the inbox's keeper: it is YOUR job to keep it tidy. `archive` stale, superseded, consumed, or no-longer-relevant items so they leave the default view; use `complete` only when an item records work that was genuinely concluded and merits a conclusion comment. Conclusion comments should state the mathematical result in human-readable language (LaTeX for formulas), not just a code changelog (see the horizon-inbox skill).
- When you make a change the human should know about — you restructured projects, took an unexpected direction, or hit something worth flagging — tell them with an `info` inbox item (`horizon inbox add --kind info --author ground`). It is purely a notice and never affects what runs.
- Tasks are shared, not human-only: you may add, set status/priority, comment, or remove tasks through the `"$HORIZON_BIN" task` CLI when it helps keep the plan honest (and a task is inferred on demand from a roadmap milestone via `horizon run <roadmap_id>`). The machine only ever writes queued/running, so a task's terminal status is whatever an agent or human records. Prefer proposing substantial new work to the human via an inbox item, and keep the roadmap — not the task list — as the source of mathematical intent.
- Delegate to subagents for bounded review and upkeep (blueprint review, diff analysis, reference lookup), preferring a smaller/cheaper model for mechanical checks.
- Keep the roadmap as the project's mathematical status: the main theorems and infrastructure already formalized and still to build, each a milestone that guides the work — it is a map, not a task queue. Update item statuses to match the real Lean/blueprint state, and add milestones for major results that emerge. Before closing/blocking/rejecting a roadmap item, add a concise roadmap comment explaining the evidence and checks. If you comment on a task whose status should be changed, explicitly name the linked `roadmap_refs` that should move with it and the matching status/comment to apply. Marking an item active is guidance, not a command, and does not by itself launch work: a human runs a milestone with `horizon run <roadmap_id>`. If you think work should start, say so in an inbox item to the human.
- Treat the opened inbox below as input for this round only. Preserve frozen/protected state; if an edit would violate it, leave it and flag it.

Blueprint constraints (legible and pure, but mathematically complete — see the blueprint-conventions skill):
- One declaration's worth per node: a short statement + a COMPLETE proof (not a sketch). Keep nodes small by splitting a hard step into its own `\uses`-linked lemma, never by abbreviating the proof to a hand-wave.
- Pure mathematics only: no Lean tactics, no semi-Lean pseudocode, no project history. Do not restate Lean source as prose. Add a `\uses` edge rather than re-explaining a dependency.
- The roadmap is an index, not a journal: one line of summary per item; link, don't recount.
- Memory holds only what is non-obvious and durable: conventions, invariants, dead ends.

# This is a RECONCILE Ground
A Horizon session just ran. Do a bounded but SKEPTICAL review of its report and project diff (the `project-git` skill), then reconcile blueprints/roadmap/memory with what actually changed. Read the report as a claim to verify against the diff and Lean state, not a summary to take on trust: separate what was genuinely proved from what was deferred, weakened, or stubbed. Watch for avoidance — a `sorry`/`admit`/placeholder or new `axiom` left behind, the easy sub-goals closed while the hard core is punted, an artificial case split that dodges the real difficulty, or a statement quietly weakened to pass. When the report says something like 'this is multi-session work, I stopped because …', judge from the evidence whether that is a real mathematical blocker or a hard step being avoided, and record your honest read (an `info`/`memory` inbox item or a roadmap comment) so the project does not quietly stagnate behind plausible-sounding excuses. Focus on correctness, consistency, and workspace hygiene; avoid long proof search or exhaustive theorem triage.

# Skills
Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path), e.g. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --json` — a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
Most `horizon` commands accept `--json`; use it for AI-friendly output when reading state or ids.
Capability know-how lives in skill files under the workspace `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude Code surfaces them automatically; on other engines read the files directly). Consult the relevant one before acting (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG):
- blueprint-conventions — The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
- horizon-commit — Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
- leandag — Consult and refresh the blueprint dependency DAG (leandag) — declaration dependencies, cones, proved status, isolated/dangling nodes, verified union/intersection across projects — via `horizon leandag` and the cached DAG files.
- leansearch — Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
- mathlib-conventions — Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
- project-git — How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
- references — The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR).
- subagents — How the Ground agent delegates to native subagents to divide review/upkeep work — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, model tiers, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
- task-status — What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You never commit.** The orchestrator writes the integration commit for each
  session automatically. You *read* history; you do not commit project or
  workspace repos manually, and there is no "project VCS" to reconcile.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
To inspect Archon's history, drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration this node formalizes. Keep it 1-to-1: one
  blueprint node ↔ one Lean declaration, signatures matching.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. If a Lean helper exists with no math counterpart,
  write its LaTeX statement so the 1-to-1 correspondence holds.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One declaration's worth per node.** Don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

857	\begin{lemma}[Descent survives base change of the cover]
858	  \label{lem:baseChangeInclude_mem_descentClasses}

863	  \(\kappa_E^{*}\lambda \in \mathrm{Desc}(C, E_{A'})\).
864	\end{lemma}
865	\begin{proof}
866	  \leanok
867	  The two coprojections of the double cover of \(E_{A'}\)
868	  (Definition~\ref{def:doubleInl_doubleInr}), composed with \(\kappa_E\), are two
869	  homomorphisms of \(A\)-algebras \(B_E \to B_{E_{A'}} \otimes_{A'} B_{E_{A'}}\) (both factor
870	  through the \(A\)-algebra structure of the target inherited from \(A \to A'\)): namely
871	  \(\mathrm{inl} \circ \kappa_E\) and \(\mathrm{inr} \circ \kappa_E\), sending \(b \mapsto
872	  (1 \otimes b) \otimes 1\), respectively \(b \mapsto 1 \otimes (1 \otimes b)\), under the
873	  carrier identifications. By the keystone (Theorem~\ref{thm:relPicAlgMap_congr}), applied with

877	  (\kappa_E^{*}\lambda) = \mathrm{inr}^{*}(\kappa_E^{*}\lambda)\), the descent condition for
878	  \(\kappa_E^{*}\lambda\) on \(E_{A'}\).

1035	\section{Separatedness I: pullback along the projection is injective}
1036	
1037	The plus construction of the preceding sections is a legitimate computation of the \'etale
1038	sheafification only because \emph{one} plus suffices, and that rests on the relative Picard
1039	functor being separated for the \'etale topology. This section establishes the geometric heart
1040	of that separatedness: pullback of Picard classes along the projection
1041	\(\mathrm{pr} \colon C \otimes T \to T\) is \emph{injective}, for every test object \(T\).
1042	
1043	Throughout, \(k\) is a field and \(C\) is an object of \(\Over(\Spec k)\) which is proper,
1044	geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over \(k\). We recall from elsewhere in
1045	this project the definitional Picard layer on a scheme \(X\): a \emph{pointed cover}
1046	\(\mathcal U\) of \(X\) assigns to each point \(x \in X\) an open \(\mathcal U(x) \ni x\);
1047	pointed covers are ordered by pointwise inclusion (a \emph{refinement}
1048	\(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\)), with pointwise intersection as meet; a \emph{unit \v Cech
1049	\(1\)-cocycle} \(\gamma\) on \(\mathcal U\) assigns to each pair \(x,y\) a unit
1050	\(\gamma_{xy} \in \struct X(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) satisfying
1051	\(\gamma_{xy}\gamma_{yz} = \gamma_{xz}\) on triple intersections; \(\check H^1(\mathcal U)\)
1052	is the group of such cocycles modulo coboundaries \((\delta\alpha)_{xy} =
1053	\alpha_x\alpha_y^{-1}\) for families of units \(\alpha_x \in
1054	\struct X(\mathcal U(x))^{\times}\); restriction along a refinement is a group homomorphism
1055	\(\check H^1(\mathcal U) \to \check H^1(\mathcal W)\); and the Picard group
1056	\(\Pic(X)\) is the colimit of the \(\check H^1(\mathcal U)\) along the (directed) refinement
1057	order, with structure maps written \([\mathcal U, a] \in \Pic(X)\), and with contravariant
1058	pullback \(f^{*} \colon \Pic(Y) \to \Pic(X)\) along a morphism \(f \colon X \to Y\), computed
1059	by pulling back the cover pointwise and the cocycle by \(f^{\sharp}\).
1060	
1061	\begin{lemma}[Separation for unit sections]
1062	  \label{lem:units_separation}
1063	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsRestrict_eq_of_locally_eq}
1064	  \leanok
1065	  Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(V \subseteq X\) open, and \((W_i)_{i \in I}\) a family of opens
1066	  with \(W_i \subseteq V\) and \(V \subseteq \bigcup_i W_i\). If two units
1067	  \(s, t \in \struct X(V)^{\times}\) satisfy \(s|_{W_i} = t|_{W_i}\) for all \(i\), then
1068	  \(s = t\).
1069	\end{lemma}
1070	\begin{proof}
1071	  \leanok
1072	  Units are equal once their underlying sections are, and the underlying sections agree on a
1073	  cover of \(V\); conclude by the separation half of the sheaf axiom for \(\struct X\).
1074	\end{proof}

1077	  \label{lem:units_gluing}

1081	  with \(W_i \subseteq V\) and \(V \subseteq \bigcup_i W_i\). Any family of units
1082	  \(u_i \in \struct X(W_i)^{\times}\) with \(u_i|_{W_i \cap W_j} = u_j|_{W_i \cap W_j}\) for
1083	  all \(i,j\) glues to a unit \(s \in \struct X(V)^{\times}\) with \(s|_{W_i} = u_i\).

1089	  \((u_i^{-1})\); by the sheaf axiom they glue to sections \(s, s' \in \struct X(V)\)
1090	  respectively. The products \(s s'\) and \(s' s\) restrict to \(1\) on every \(W_i\), hence

1100	  \(u \in \struct X(U)^{\times}\), restricting \(u\) to \(V\) and then to \(W\) is

1102	\end{lemma}

1104	  \leanok

1108	\begin{theorem}[Refinement injectivity in degree one]
1109	  \label{thm:unitsRes_injective}
1110	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsRes_injective}
1111	  \leanok
1112	  Let \(X\) be a scheme and \(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\) pointed covers of \(X\). Then
1113	  restriction \(\check H^1(\mathcal U) \to \check H^1(\mathcal W)\) is injective.
1114	\end{theorem}

1116	  \leanok
1117	  \uses{lem:units_separation, lem:units_gluing, lem:unitsRestrict_trans}
1118	  Restriction is a group homomorphism, so it suffices to show a cocycle \(\gamma\) on
1119	  \(\mathcal U\) whose restriction to \(\mathcal W\) is a coboundary, say
1120	  \(\gamma_{zz'}|_{\mathcal W(z) \cap \mathcal W(z')} = \alpha_z \alpha_{z'}^{-1}\) with
1121	  \(\alpha_z \in \struct X(\mathcal W(z))^{\times}\), is itself a coboundary. Fix a point
1122	  \(i\) and consider, for each point \(z\), the \emph{comparison unit}
1123	  \[ s_{i,z} := \alpha_z \cdot \gamma_{iz}^{-1}
1124	     \in \struct X\bigl(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(z)\bigr)^{\times}, \]
1125	  which makes sense since \(\mathcal W(z) \subseteq \mathcal U(z)\). On the overlap
1126	  \((\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(z)) \cap (\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(z'))\) the cocycle
1127	  identity \(\gamma_{iz}\gamma_{zz'} = \gamma_{iz'}\) at \((i,z,z')\) and the coboundary
1128	  relation \(\alpha_z \gamma_{zz'} = \alpha_{z'}\) give
1129	  \(s_{i,z'} = \alpha_z\gamma_{zz'}\cdot(\gamma_{iz}\gamma_{zz'})^{-1} = s_{i,z}\). Since
1130	  every point \(w \in \mathcal U(i)\) lies in \(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(w)\), these
1131	  opens cover \(\mathcal U(i)\), and by gluing (Lemma~\ref{lem:units_gluing}) there is
1132	  \(\beta_i \in \struct X(\mathcal U(i))^{\times}\) with
1133	  \(\beta_i|_{\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(z)} = s_{i,z}\) for all \(z\). Finally, for any
1134	  \(i, j\), on each member \(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal U(j) \cap \mathcal W(z)\) of a cover
1135	  of \(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal U(j)\) we compute, using the cocycle identity at
1136	  \((i,j,z)\),
1137	  \[ \beta_i \gamma_{ij} = \alpha_z \gamma_{iz}^{-1}\gamma_{ij}
1138	       = \alpha_z \gamma_{jz}^{-1} = \beta_j , \]
1139	  so \(\beta_i \gamma_{ij} = \beta_j\) on \(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal U(j)\) by separation
1140	  (Lemma~\ref{lem:units_separation}); that is, \(\gamma = \delta(\beta^{-1})\) is a
1141	  coboundary.

1198	\begin{theorem}[Sections over an affine open pull back bijectively]
1199	  \label{thm:isIso_appLE_snd}
1200	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isIso_appLE_snd}
1201	  \leanok
1202	  Let \(T\) be an object of \(\Over(\Spec k)\) and \(V \subseteq T\) an affine open. Then
1203	  pullback of sections along the second projection
1204	  \(\mathrm{pr} \colon C \otimes T \to T\) is an isomorphism
1205	  \[ \Gamma(T, V) \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\; \Gamma\bigl(C \otimes T,\
1206	     \mathrm{pr}^{-1}V\bigr). \]
1207	\end{theorem}
1208	\begin{proof}
1209	  \leanok
1210	  \uses{lem:flat_of_field, cor:curve_sections}
1211	  The underlying scheme of \(C \otimes T\) is the fibre product
1212	  \(C \times_{\Spec k} T\). Since \(C\) is proper over the field \(k\), its underlying space
1213	  is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and \(T \to \Spec k\) is flat
1214	  (Lemma~\ref{lem:flat_of_field}); therefore the canonical square of section rings
1215	  \[ \begin{array}{ccc}
1216	     \Gamma(\Spec k, \struct{}) & \longrightarrow & \Gamma(C, \struct C) \\
1217	     \downarrow & & \downarrow \\
1218	     \Gamma(T, V) & \longrightarrow & \Gamma(C \otimes T, \mathrm{pr}^{-1}V)
1219	     \end{array} \]
1220	  --- with the affine slots at \(\Spec k\) (all of it) and at \(V \subseteq T\), and the
1221	  quasi-compact quasi-separated slot at all of \(C\) --- is a pushout of commutative rings:
1222	  the flat-base-change theorem for sections of fibre products. The top edge is an
1223	  isomorphism, \(\Gamma(C, \struct C) = k\) (Corollary~\ref{cor:curve_sections}); a pushout

9	/-!
10	# The transition cocycle of a locally trivialized module, and its Picard class
11	
12	Let `A` be a commutative ring, `N` an `A`-module, and `f : ι → A` a finite family with
13	localization models `S i`, `T i j`, `W i j k` away from the single, double and triple
14	products as in `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LocalizationCocycle`.  Given trivializations
15	`e i : S i ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[S i] S i` on the members of the cover, this file:
16	
17	* forms the **transition cocycle** `trivializationCocycle e i j : (T i j)ˣ` — the
18	  transition unit between the two pushforwards of `e i` and `e j` to the overlap — and
19	  shows it is a Čech cover cocycle (`isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle`), the diagonal
20	  and cocycle conditions being instances of the transition-unit calculus of
21	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.BaseChangeTrivialization` plus the uniqueness of `A`-algebra
22	  maps out of localizations;
23	* assembles the componentwise trivializations into one over the cover algebra
24	  `B := ∀ i, S i` (`Module.piTrivialization`);
25	* proves the **descent identification** (`picClass_trivializationCocycle`): the Picard
26	  class of the descent cocycle associated with the transition cocycle is the class of
27	  `N` itself.  The compatibility of the assembled trivialization with the twisted
28	  descent datum reduces, through the identification `B ⊗[A] B ≃ ∀ p, T p.1 p.2`, to the
29	  defining property of the transition units, and uniqueness of descent
30	  (`Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended`) identifies the descended module with `N`.
31	
32	This is the algebraic heart of the surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism
33	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic_surjective`).
34	-/

36	universe u
37	
38	open TensorProduct
39	
40	/-! ## Assembling componentwise trivializations over a finite product -/
41	
42	namespace Module
43	
44	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
45	variable {S : ι → Type u} [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra A (S i)]
46	variable {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
47	
48	/-- The canonical `A`-linear distribution of a base change over a finite product of
49	`A`-algebras. -/
50	noncomputable def piBaseChangeDistrib :
51	    ((∀ i, S i) ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[A] ∀ i, S i ⊗[A] N :=
52	  (TensorProduct.comm A _ _).trans ((TensorProduct.piRight A A N S).trans
53	    (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ TensorProduct.comm A N (S i)))
54	
55	@[simp]
56	lemma piBaseChangeDistrib_tmul (b : ∀ i, S i) (n : N) :
57	    piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S) (b ⊗ₜ[A] n) = fun i ↦ b i ⊗ₜ[A] n := by
58	  funext i
59	  simp [piBaseChangeDistrib, TensorProduct.piRight_apply]
60	
61	variable (e : ∀ i, (S i ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[S i] S i)
62	
63	/-- The `A`-linear map underlying `piTrivialization`: `n ↦ (i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n))`. -/
64	private noncomputable def piTrivializationBase : N →ₗ[A] ∀ i, S i where
65	  toFun n i := e i (1 ⊗ₜ n)
66	  map_add' n m := by
67	    funext i
68	    simp only [Pi.add_apply, TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add]
69	  map_smul' a n := by
70	    funext i
71	    simp only [RingHom.id_apply, Pi.smul_apply, TensorProduct.tmul_smul]
72	    exact LinearMapClass.map_smul_of_tower (e i) a _
73	
74	/-- Componentwise trivializations of `N` over a finite family of `A`-algebras assemble
75	into a trivialization over the product algebra, sending `1 ⊗ₜ n` to
76	`fun i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n)` (`piTrivialization_one_tmul`). -/
77	noncomputable def piTrivialization :
78	    ((∀ i, S i) ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[∀ i, S i] ∀ i, S i := by
79	  refine LinearEquiv.ofBijective
80	    (LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e)) ?_
81	  have key : ⇑(LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e))
82	      = (fun v i ↦ e i (v i)) ∘ ⇑(piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S)) := by
83	    funext x
84	    induction x with
85	    | zero => exact funext fun i ↦ by simp
86	    | tmul b n =>
87	        funext i
88	        simp only [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, Function.comp_apply,
89	          piBaseChangeDistrib_tmul]
90	        have hb : (b i ⊗ₜ[A] n : S i ⊗[A] N) = b i • ((1 : S i) ⊗ₜ[A] n) := by
91	          rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
92	        rw [hb, map_smul]
93	        simp [piTrivializationBase, smul_eq_mul]
94	    | add x y hx hy =>
95	        rw [map_add, hx, hy]
96	        funext i
97	        simp only [Function.comp_apply, map_add, Pi.add_apply]
98	  rw [key]
99	  exact ((Equiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ (e i).toEquiv).bijective).comp
100	    (piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S)).bijective
101	
102	@[simp]
103	lemma piTrivialization_one_tmul (n : N) :
104	    piTrivialization e (1 ⊗ₜ n) = fun i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n) := by
105	  change LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e) (1 ⊗ₜ n) = _
106	  rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]
107	  rfl

128	variable (e : ∀ i, (S i ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[S i] S i)

130	/-- The **transition cocycle** of a family of trivializations on a finite localization
131	cover: on each overlap, the transition unit between the pushforwards of the two
132	trivializations. -/
133	noncomputable def trivializationCocycle (i j : ι) : (T i j)ˣ :=
134	  transitionUnit (trivializationPush (inclLeft f S T i j) (e i))
135	    (trivializationPush (inclRight f S T i j) (e j))

137	/-- The defining property of the transition cocycle on the tensors `1 ⊗ₜ n`. -/
138	lemma trivializationCocycle_mul (i j : ι) (n : N) :
139	    (trivializationCocycle f S T e i j).val * inclLeft f S T i j (e i (1 ⊗ₜ n))
140	      = inclRight f S T i j (e j (1 ⊗ₜ n)) := by
141	  have h := transitionUnit_mul_apply (trivializationPush (inclLeft f S T i j) (e i))
142	    (trivializationPush (inclRight f S T i j) (e j)) (1 ⊗ₜ n)
143	  rwa [trivializationPush_one_tmul, trivializationPush_one_tmul] at h
144	
145	/-- The transition cocycle is a Čech cover cocycle: the diagonal and cocycle conditions
146	follow from the transition-unit calculus and uniqueness of `A`-algebra maps out of
147	localizations. -/
148	theorem isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle :
149	    IsCoverCocycle (f := f) (S := S) (W := W) (trivializationCocycle f S T e) := by
150	  constructor
151	  · -- diagonal: the two pushforwards to `T i i` agree, so the transition unit is `1`
152	    intro i
153	    have hlr : inclLeft f S T i i = inclRight f S T i i :=
154	      (IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton (Submonoid.powers (f i))).elim _ _
155	    have h1 : trivializationCocycle f S T e i i = 1 := by
156	      rw [trivializationCocycle, hlr, transitionUnit_self]
157	    rw [h1, Units.val_one, map_one]
158	  · -- cocycle: push all three transition units to the triple overlap and telescope
159	    intro i j k
160	    -- canonical pushforwards of the three trivializations to the triple overlap
161	    set ρi : S i →ₐ[A] W i j k := (face₁₂ f T W i j k).comp (inclLeft f S T i j) with hρi
162	    set ρj : S j →ₐ[A] W i j k := (face₁₂ f T W i j k).comp (inclRight f S T i j) with hρj
163	    set ρk : S k →ₐ[A] W i j k := (face₂₃ f T W i j k).comp (inclRight f S T j k) with hρk
164	    have key : Units.map (face₂₃ f T W i j k).toRingHom.toMonoidHom
165	          (trivializationCocycle f S T e j k)
166	        * Units.map (face₁₂ f T W i j k).toRingHom.toMonoidHom
167	            (trivializationCocycle f S T e i j)
168	        = Units.map (face₁₃ f T W i j k).toRingHom.toMonoidHom
169	            (trivializationCocycle f S T e i k) := by
170	      rw [trivializationCocycle, trivializationCocycle, trivializationCocycle,
171	        ← map_transitionUnit, ← map_transitionUnit, ← map_transitionUnit,
172	        trivializationPush_trivializationPush, trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
173	        trivializationPush_trivializationPush, trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
174	        trivializationPush_trivializationPush, trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
175	        show (face₂₃ f T W i j k).comp (inclLeft f S T j k) = ρj from
176	          (IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton (Submonoid.powers (f j))).elim _ _,
177	        show (face₂₃ f T W i j k).comp (inclRight f S T j k) = ρk from rfl,
178	        show (face₁₂ f T W i j k).comp (inclLeft f S T i j) = ρi from rfl,
179	        show (face₁₂ f T W i j k).comp (inclRight f S T i j) = ρj from rfl,
180	        show (face₁₃ f T W i j k).comp (inclLeft f S T i k) = ρi from
181	          (IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton (Submonoid.powers (f i))).elim _ _,
182	        show (face₁₃ f T W i j k).comp (inclRight f S T i k) = ρk from
183	          (IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton (Submonoid.powers (f k))).elim _ _]
184	      exact transitionUnit_mul_transitionUnit _ _ _
185	    have hval := congrArg Units.val key
186	    simp only [Units.val_mul, Units.coe_map] at hval
187	    exact hval
188	
189	/-! ## The Picard class of the transition cocycle -/
190	
191	variable [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
192	
193	/-- **Descent identification for locally trivialized modules**: the Picard class of the
194	descent cocycle associated with the transition cocycle of a family of trivializations of
195	`N` is the class of `N`.  The assembled trivialization over the cover algebra
196	intertwines the twisted descent datum of the transition cocycle with the canonical datum
197	on `B ⊗[A] N` — componentwise this is the defining property of the transition units —
198	so uniqueness of descent identifies the descended module with `N`. -/
199	theorem picClass_trivializationCocycle [Module.Invertible A N]
200	    [Module.FaithfullyFlat A (∀ i, S i)] :
201	    (isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit f S T W
202	        (isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle f S T W e)).picClass
203	      = CommRing.Pic.mk A N := by
204	  set B := ∀ i, S i with hB
205	  set u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ := cocycleUnit f S T (trivializationCocycle f S T e) with hu'
206	  set hu := isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit f S T W
207	    (isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle f S T W e)
208	  set ψ : (B ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] B := piTrivialization e with hψ
209	  -- the values of the assembled trivialization on `1 ⊗ₜ n` lie in the descended module
210	  have hkey : ∀ n : N,
211	      u.val * descentIncl₁ A B (ψ (1 ⊗ₜ n)) = descentIncl₂ A B (ψ (1 ⊗ₜ n)) := by
212	    intro n
213	    apply (piDoubleEquiv f S T).injective
214	    rw [map_mul, piDoubleEquiv_cocycleUnit_val, piDoubleEquiv_descentIncl₁,
215	      piDoubleEquiv_descentIncl₂]
216	    funext p
217	    rw [Pi.mul_apply]
218	    have hval : ψ (1 ⊗ₜ n) = fun i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n) := piTrivialization_one_tmul e n
219	    rw [hval]
220	    exact trivializationCocycle_mul f S T e p.1 p.2 n
221	  -- the assembled trivialization intertwines the two descent data
222	  have he : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] N,
223	      (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).coaction (ψ x)
224	        = ((ψ : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] B).restrictScalars A).baseChange B
225	            ((DescentDatum.baseChange A B N).coaction x) := by
226	    intro x
227	    induction x with
228	    | zero => simp
229	    | tmul b n =>
230	        have hb : (b ⊗ₜ[A] n : B ⊗[A] N) = b • ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] n) := by
231	          rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
232	        set s : B := ψ (1 ⊗ₜ n) with hs
233	        have hψb : ψ (b ⊗ₜ n) = b * s := by
234	          rw [hb, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]
235	        rw [hψb, ofUnit_coaction, unitCoaction_apply, DescentDatum.baseChange_coaction,
236	          LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul]
237	        have hmul : ((b * s) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B) : B ⊗[A] B)
238	            = (b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * (s ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) := by
239	          rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one]
240	        have hkey' : u.val * (s ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) = (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] s := hkey n
241	        calc u.val * (b * s) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)
242	            = (b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * (u.val * (s ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B))) := by
243	              rw [hmul]; ring
244	          _ = (b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] s) := by rw [hkey']
245	          _ = b ⊗ₜ[A] ψ ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] n) := by
246	              rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one, one_mul, hs]
247	    | add x y hx hy => rw [map_add, map_add, map_add, map_add, hx, hy]
248	  -- uniqueness of descent identifies the descended module with `N`
249	  have equivN : N ≃ₗ[A] hu.descended :=
250	    (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).equivDescended ψ he
251	  exact CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨equivN.symm⟩
252	
253	end IsLocalization.AwayCover

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine
7	
8	/-!
9	# The Čech–Picard descent homomorphism of an affine scheme
10	
11	Assembly of the choice-independent Picard classes of
12	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine` into the injective group homomorphism
13	
14	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`
15	
16	for an affine scheme `X` — the homomorphism half of the Čech–Picard dictionary
17	(mathlib's `RingTheory.PicardGroup` TODO "exhibit isomorphism with `H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`").
18	Injectivity (`CechPic.toPic_injective`) is refinement injectivity: a trivial descent
19	class makes the descent unit a coboundary, which glues back to a coboundary on the
20	pointed cover itself.  Surjectivity — trivializations of an invertible module on a basic
21	cover — is the remaining half of the dictionary.
22	-/
23	
24	set_option autoImplicit false
25	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000
26	
27	universe u
28	
29	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
30	
31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
32	
33	namespace Scheme
34	
35	/-! ## The descent homomorphism -/
36	
37	namespace CechPic
38	
39	open PointedCover
40	
41	variable (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
42	
43	/-- The underlying function of `CechPic.toPic`: descend along a chosen basic refinement
44	of a chosen representative. -/
45	noncomputable def toPicFun : X.CechPic → CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤) :=
46	  Quotient.lift
47	    (fun p : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 ↦
48	      (BasicRefinement.nonempty p.1).some.pic p.2.out)
49	    (by
50	      rintro ⟨𝒰, a⟩ ⟨𝒱, b⟩ ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
51	      -- The restrictions of the chosen representatives to `𝒲` are cohomologous:
52	      -- their `H¹` classes are `unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b`.
53	      refine BasicRefinement.pic_congr h₁ h₂ _ _ ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ?_)
54	      have ha : a.out.class = a := Quot.out_eq a
55	      have hb : b.out.class = b := Quot.out_eq b
56	      calc (a.out.res fun x ↦ homOfLE (h₁ x)).class
57	          = unitsRes h₁ a.out.class := rfl
58	        _ = unitsRes h₂ b.out.class := by rw [ha, hb]; exact e
59	        _ = (b.out.res fun x ↦ homOfLE (h₂ x)).class := rfl)
60	
61	variable {X}
62	
63	@[simp]
64	lemma toPicFun_mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰)
65	    (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) : toPicFun X (CechPic.mk 𝒰 γ.class) = P.pic γ := by
66	  -- The chosen data compare to `(P, γ)` by `BasicRefinement.pic_congr` with `𝒲 := 𝒰`
67	  -- (the representative `Quot.out (γ.class)` is cohomologous to `γ`).
68	  show (BasicRefinement.nonempty 𝒰).some.pic (Quot.out γ.class) = P.pic γ
69	  refine BasicRefinement.pic_congr (𝒲 := 𝒰) le_rfl le_rfl _ _
70	    ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ?_)
71	  have hγ : (Quot.out γ.class).class = γ.class := Quot.out_eq γ.class
72	  calc ((Quot.out γ.class).res fun x ↦ homOfLE ((le_rfl : 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) x)).class
73	      = unitsRes le_rfl (Quot.out γ.class).class := rfl
74	    _ = unitsRes le_rfl γ.class := by rw [hγ]
75	    _ = (γ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE ((le_rfl : 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) x)).class := rfl
76	
77	variable (X)
78	
79	/-- **The Čech–Picard descent homomorphism** of an affine scheme: from the definitional
80	Čech Picard group to mathlib's Picard group of the global sections, by faithfully flat
81	descent along finite basic covers. -/
82	noncomputable def toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤) where
83	  toFun := toPicFun X
84	  map_one' := by
85	    have h : (1 : X.CechPic) = CechPic.mk ⊤ (OneCocycle.class 1) := rfl
86	    obtain ⟨P⟩ := BasicRefinement.nonempty (⊤ : X.PointedCover)
87	    rw [h, toPicFun_mk _ _ P]
88	    exact P.pic_one
89	  map_mul' x y := by
90	    induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
91	    induction y using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
92	    obtain ⟨P⟩ := BasicRefinement.nonempty (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱)
93	    induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
94	    induction b using Quot.ind with | _ δ =>
95	    rw [CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf]
96	    have hprod : (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (Quot.mk _ γ)
97	          * unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ≤ 𝒱) (Quot.mk _ δ) : X.unitsH1 (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱))
98	        = ((γ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE ((inf_le_left : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) x))
99	            * (δ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE ((inf_le_right : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ≤ 𝒱) x))).class := rfl
100	    have h1 : (Quot.mk _ γ : X.unitsH1 𝒰) = γ.class := rfl
101	    have h2 : (Quot.mk _ δ : X.unitsH1 𝒱) = δ.class := rfl
102	    rw [hprod, h1, h2, toPicFun_mk _ _ P,
103	      toPicFun_mk _ _ (P.ofLE inf_le_left), toPicFun_mk _ _ (P.ofLE inf_le_right),
104	      BasicRefinement.pic_ofLE inf_le_left P γ, BasicRefinement.pic_ofLE inf_le_right P δ,
105	      BasicRefinement.pic_mul]
106	
107	variable {X}
108	
109	@[simp]
110	lemma toPic_mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) :
111	    toPic X (CechPic.mk 𝒰 γ.class) = P.pic γ :=
112	  toPicFun_mk 𝒰 γ P
113	
114	/-- **Injectivity of the descent homomorphism**: refinement injectivity for the Čech
115	Picard group against mathlib's Picard group. -/
116	theorem toPic_injective : Function.Injective (toPic X) := by
117	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_one]
118	  intro x hx
119	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
120	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
121	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := BasicRefinement.nonempty 𝒰
122	  rw [show Quot.mk _ γ = OneCocycle.class γ from rfl] at hx ⊢
123	  rw [toPic_mk 𝒰 γ P] at hx
124	  rw [BasicRefinement.class_eq_one_of_pic_eq_one P γ hx]
125	  exact CechPic.mk_one 𝒰
126	
127	end CechPic
128	end Scheme
129	
130	end AlgebraicGeometry

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

6	import Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup
7	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.Free
8	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.BaseChange
9	
10	/-!
11	# Invertible modules are Zariski-locally trivial
12	
13	Let `A` be a commutative ring and `N` an invertible `A`-module.  This file proves the
14	commutative-algebra form of the statement "an invertible module is Zariski-locally free":
15	
16	* `Module.Free.tensor_of_localizedModule_away`: if the standard localized module
17	  `LocalizedModule.Away r N` is free over `Localization.Away r`, then `S ⊗[A] N` is free
18	  over `S` for **any** localization model `S` of `A` away from `r`.
19	* `Module.Invertible.exists_notMem_tensor_free`: for every prime `p` of `A` there is an
20	  `f ∉ p` such that `N` trivializes away from `f`.  This is the local-to-global heart:
21	  invertible modules are finitely presented, their localization at `p` is free over the
22	  local ring `A_p` (finite flat over local is free), and freeness spreads out from the
23	  prime to a principal open neighbourhood
24	  (`Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers`).
25	* `Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top`: the trivializing elements `f` span the
26	  unit ideal, i.e. the principal opens `D(f)` on which `N` trivializes cover `Spec A`.
27	
28	This is the "invertible modules are Zariski-locally trivial" brick feeding the
29	surjectivity half of the Čech–Picard dictionary in
30	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechPicSurjective`: it produces the finite localization cover
31	on which an invertible module admits trivializations, whose transition units
32	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.BaseChangeTrivialization`) form the Čech 1-cocycle
33	presenting its class.
34	
35	**Extraction candidate.**  This file is mathlib-PR-shaped: it discharges the TODO in
36	`Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup` that invertible modules are Zariski-locally free, using
37	only `Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.Free` and the Picard-group instances.
38	
39	Everything is pinned to a single universe `u`, matching the descent development in
40	`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent`.
41	-/
42	
43	universe u
44	
45	open TensorProduct
46	
47	namespace Module
48	
49	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
50	
51	/-- Transport of freeness from the standard localized module `LocalizedModule.Away r N`
52	to the base change `S ⊗[A] N` for ANY localization model `S` of `A` away from `r`. -/
53	theorem Free.tensor_of_localizedModule_away (r : A)
54	    [Module.Free (Localization.Away r) (LocalizedModule.Away r N)]
55	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S] [IsLocalization.Away r S] :
56	    Module.Free S (S ⊗[A] N) := by
57	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away r) S :=
58	    (IsLocalization.algEquiv (Submonoid.powers r)
59	      (Localization.Away r) S).toAlgHom.toRingHom.toAlgebra
60	  haveI : IsScalarTower A (Localization.Away r) S :=
61	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun a ↦
62	      ((IsLocalization.algEquiv (Submonoid.powers r)
63	        (Localization.Away r) S).commutes a).symm
64	  haveI : Module.Free (Localization.Away r) (Localization.Away r ⊗[A] N) :=
65	    Module.Free.of_equiv (LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct (Submonoid.powers r) N)
66	  exact Module.Free.of_equiv
67	    (AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A (Localization.Away r) S S N)
68	
69	/-- An invertible module becomes free away from some element outside any given prime. -/
70	theorem Invertible.exists_notMem_tensor_free [Module.Invertible A N]
71	    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] :
72	    ∃ f ∉ p, ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S], IsLocalization.Away f S →
73	      Module.Free S (S ⊗[A] N) := by
74	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation A N := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective A N
75	  haveI : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl N) :=
76	    Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
77	  obtain ⟨r, hr, hfree, -⟩ :=
78	    Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers p.primeCompl
79	      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.primeCompl N) (Localization.AtPrime p)
80	  exact ⟨r, hr, fun S _ _ hS ↦ by
81	    haveI := hS
82	    haveI := hfree
83	    exact Free.tensor_of_localizedModule_away N r S⟩
84	
85	/-- The trivializing sections of an invertible module span the unit ideal. -/
86	theorem Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top [Module.Invertible A N] :
87	    Ideal.span {f : A | ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S], IsLocalization.Away f S →
88	      Module.Free S (S ⊗[A] N)} = ⊤ := by
89	  by_contra h
90	  obtain ⟨m, hmax, hle⟩ := Ideal.exists_le_maximal _ h
91	  haveI := hmax.isPrime
92	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfree⟩ := Invertible.exists_notMem_tensor_free N m
93	  exact hf (hle (Ideal.subset_span hfree))
94	
95	end Module

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.InvertibleLocalTrivialization
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LocalizationTrivialization
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechPicToPic
9	
10	/-!
11	# Surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism, and the dictionary
12	
13	For an affine scheme `X` this file proves surjectivity of the descent homomorphism
14	`CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)` and assembles the full
15	**Čech–Picard dictionary**
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPicEquivPic : X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`
18	
19	— the isomorphism between the definitional Čech Picard group on pointed Zariski covers
20	and mathlib's Picard group of invertible modules (the TODO of
21	`Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`: "exhibit isomorphism with `H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`").
22	
23	The route: an invertible module `N` over `Γ(X, ⊤)` trivializes on the basic open of
24	some section outside every prime, so the trivializing sections span the unit ideal
25	(`Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top`) and their basic opens cover `X`.  A
26	choice of one trivializing basic neighborhood per point is a `TrivializingFamily`; the
27	transition units of its trivializations (`Module.transitionUnit`) form a unit Čech
28	cocycle on the associated pointed cover.  Along any finite basic refinement the
29	restricted cover cocycle is the transition cocycle of the pushed-forward
30	trivializations, so its descended module is `N` itself
31	(`IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_trivializationCocycle`), and `toPic` hits the class
32	of `N`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
40	open TensorProduct
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	namespace Scheme
45	
46	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
47	
48	/-! ## Trivializing families -/
49	
50	/-- A pointed trivializing family for a module `N` over the global sections of `X`: one
51	section per point, whose basic open contains the point and carries a trivialization of
52	the base change of `N`.  Invertible modules over affine schemes always admit one
53	(`TrivializingFamily.nonempty`). -/
54	structure TrivializingFamily (X : Scheme.{u}) (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N]
55	    [Module Γ(X, ⊤) N] : Type u where
56	  /-- The trivializing section at a point. -/
57	  sec : X → Γ(X, ⊤)
58	  /-- Each point lies in the basic open of its section. -/
59	  mem_basicOpen : ∀ x, x ∈ X.basicOpen (sec x)
60	  /-- The chosen trivialization of `N` over the basic open. -/
61	  triv : ∀ x, (Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x)) ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N)
62	    ≃ₗ[Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x))] Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x))
63	
64	namespace TrivializingFamily
65	
66	variable {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module Γ(X, ⊤) N]
67	
68	/-- Every invertible module over the global sections of an affine scheme admits a
69	trivializing family: the trivializing sections span the unit ideal, so their basic
70	opens cover `X`. -/
71	theorem nonempty [IsAffine X] [Module.Invertible Γ(X, ⊤) N] :
72	    Nonempty (TrivializingFamily X N) := by
73	  have hcover :
74	      (⨆ f : {f : Γ(X, ⊤) | ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra Γ(X, ⊤) S],
75	          IsLocalization.Away f S → Module.Free S (S ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N)},
76	        X.basicOpen f.1) = ⊤ :=
77	    (isAffineOpen_top X).iSup_basicOpen_eq_self_iff.mpr
78	      (Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top N)
79	  have hex : ∀ x : X, ∃ f : Γ(X, ⊤),
80	      (∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra Γ(X, ⊤) S],
81	        IsLocalization.Away f S → Module.Free S (S ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N))
82	      ∧ x ∈ X.basicOpen f := by
83	    intro x
84	    obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (hcover.ge (trivial : x ∈ (⊤ : X.Opens)))
85	    exact ⟨f.1, f.2, hf⟩
86	  choose f hfree hmem using hex
87	  refine ⟨⟨f, hmem, fun x ↦ ?_⟩⟩
88	  haveI : Module.Free Γ(X, X.basicOpen (f x)) (Γ(X, X.basicOpen (f x)) ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N) :=
89	    hfree x Γ(X, X.basicOpen (f x)) inferInstance
90	  exact (Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv.mp this).some
91	
92	variable (F : TrivializingFamily X N)
93	
94	/-- The pointed cover underlying a trivializing family. -/
95	def cover : X.PointedCover where
96	  opens x := X.basicOpen (F.sec x)
97	  mem_opens := F.mem_basicOpen
98	
99	@[simp]
100	lemma cover_opens (x : X) : F.cover.opens x = X.basicOpen (F.sec x) :=
101	  rfl
102	
103	section transition
104	
105	variable [IsAffine X]
106	
107	/-- The transition cocycle of the trivializing family: on each double overlap, the
108	transition unit between the pushforwards of the trivializations at the two points. -/
109	noncomputable def transition (x y : X) : Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))ˣ :=
110	  IsLocalization.AwayCover.trivializationCocycle F.sec
111	    (fun x ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x)))
112	    (fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))) F.triv x y
113	
114	/-- The transition units form a Čech cover cocycle on the (infinite) family of
115	trivializing basic opens. -/
116	lemma isCoverCocycle_transition :
117	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.IsCoverCocycle (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
118	      (S := fun x ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x)))
119	      (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y)))
120	      (W := fun x y z ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z))))
121	      F.transition :=
122	  IsLocalization.AwayCover.isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle F.sec _ _ _ F.triv
123	
124	/-- The cocycle identity for the transition units, restricted to any common open. -/
125	lemma transition_mul (x y z : X) {T : X.Opens}
126	    (hxy : T ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))
127	    (hyz : T ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec y * F.sec z))
128	    (hxz : T ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec z)) :
129	    X.unitsRestrict hxy (F.transition x y) * X.unitsRestrict hyz (F.transition y z)
130	      = X.unitsRestrict hxz (F.transition x z) := by
131	  -- restrictions from the double overlaps to the triple overlap
132	  have h₁₂ : X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z))
133	      ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y) :=
134	    X.basicOpen_le_of_dvd ⟨F.sec z, by ring⟩
135	  have h₂₃ : X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z))
136	      ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec y * F.sec z) :=
137	    X.basicOpen_le_of_dvd ⟨F.sec x, by ring⟩
138	  have h₁₃ : X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z))
139	      ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec z) :=
140	    X.basicOpen_le_of_dvd ⟨F.sec y, by ring⟩
141	  -- the common open sits inside the triple overlap
142	  have hT : T ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z)) := by
143	    rw [X.basicOpen_mul, X.basicOpen_mul]
144	    exact le_inf (hxy.trans ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_left))
145	      (le_inf (hxy.trans ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_right))
146	        (hyz.trans ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_right)))
147	  -- the cover cocycle identity, with the face maps rewritten as restrictions
148	  have hc := (F.isCoverCocycle_transition).cocycle x y z
149	  rw [show IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₂₃ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
150	        (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y)))
151	        (W := fun x y z ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z)))) x y z
152	      = X.basicRes _ _ h₂₃ from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _,
153	    show IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₁₂ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
154	        (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y)))
155	        (W := fun x y z ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z)))) x y z
156	      = X.basicRes _ _ h₁₂ from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _,
157	    show IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₁₃ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
158	        (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y)))
159	        (W := fun x y z ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z)))) x y z
160	      = X.basicRes _ _ h₁₃ from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _] at hc
161	  -- lift to units on the triple overlap
162	  have hu : X.unitsRestrict h₂₃ (F.transition y z) * X.unitsRestrict h₁₂ (F.transition x y)
163	      = X.unitsRestrict h₁₃ (F.transition x z) := Units.ext hc
164	  -- restrict to `T` and collapse the composed restrictions
165	  have e := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict hT) hu
166	  rw [map_mul, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict,
167	    unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e
168	  exact (mul_comm _ _).trans e
169	
170	/-- The unit Čech cocycle of a trivializing family on its pointed cover: the value on
171	`T ≤ D(sec x) ⊓ D(sec y)` is the restriction of the transition unit. -/
172	noncomputable def cocycle : X.unitsCocycle F.cover where
173	  ev x y _ a b :=
174	    X.unitsRestrict ((le_inf a.le b.le).trans (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec x) (F.sec y)).ge)
175	      (F.transition x y)
176	  ev_precomp _ _ _ _ _ _ _ := unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict _ _ _
177	  ev_trans x y z _ a b c :=
178	    F.transition_mul x y z
179	      ((le_inf a.le b.le).trans (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec x) (F.sec y)).ge)
180	      ((le_inf b.le c.le).trans (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec y) (F.sec z)).ge)
181	      ((le_inf a.le c.le).trans (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec x) (F.sec z)).ge)
182	
183	/-- The pair values of the trivializing cocycle are the restricted transition units. -/
184	lemma cocycle_unitsEvInf (x y : X) :
185	    unitsEvInf F.cocycle x y
186	      = X.unitsRestrict (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec x) (F.sec y)).ge (F.transition x y) :=
187	  rfl
188	
189	/-! ## The Picard class along a basic refinement -/
190	
191	/-- The trivializations of the family, pushed forward to a basic refinement of the
192	trivializing cover. -/
193	noncomputable def refTriv (P : F.cover.BasicRefinement) (i : P.ι) :
194	    (Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)) ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N)
195	      ≃ₗ[Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i))] Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)) :=
196	  Module.trivializationPush (X.basicRes _ _ (P.basicOpen_le i)) (F.triv (P.pt i))
197	
198	/-- Restricting the trivializing cocycle to a basic refinement recovers the transition
199	cocycle of the pushed trivializations. -/
200	lemma coverCocycle_eq (P : F.cover.BasicRefinement) (i j : P.ι) :
201	    P.coverCocycle F.cocycle i j
202	      = IsLocalization.AwayCover.trivializationCocycle P.r
203	          (fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
204	          (fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) (F.refTriv P) i j := by
205	  have hle : X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)
206	      ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec (P.pt i) * F.sec (P.pt j)) :=
207	    (P.overlap_le i j).trans (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).ge
208	  have h₁ : P.coverCocycle F.cocycle i j
209	      = X.unitsRestrict hle (F.transition (P.pt i) (P.pt j)) :=
210	    unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec (P.pt i)) (F.sec (P.pt j))).ge
211	      (P.overlap_le i j) (F.transition (P.pt i) (P.pt j))
212	  rw [h₁, IsLocalization.AwayCover.trivializationCocycle, refTriv, refTriv,
213	    Module.trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
214	    Module.trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
215	    show (IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclLeft (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
216	        (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
217	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i j).comp
218	          (X.basicRes _ _ (P.basicOpen_le i))
219	      = (X.basicRes _ _ hle).comp
220	          (IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclLeft (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
221	            (S := fun x ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x)))
222	            (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))) (P.pt i) (P.pt j))
223	      from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _,
224	    show (IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclRight (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
225	        (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
226	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i j).comp
227	          (X.basicRes _ _ (P.basicOpen_le j))
228	      = (X.basicRes _ _ hle).comp
229	          (IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclRight (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
230	            (S := fun x ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x)))
231	            (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))) (P.pt i) (P.pt j))
232	      from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _,
233	    ← Module.trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
234	    ← Module.trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
235	    Module.map_transitionUnit]
236	  rfl
237	
238	/-- **Descent identification**: along any basic refinement, the Picard class of the
239	trivializing cocycle is the class of `N` itself. -/
240	theorem pic_cocycle [Module.Invertible Γ(X, ⊤) N] (P : F.cover.BasicRefinement) :
241	    P.pic F.cocycle = CommRing.Pic.mk Γ(X, ⊤) N := by
242	  letI := P.faithfullyFlat
243	  rw [P.pic_eq_picClass]
244	  refine (Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_congr _
245	      (IsLocalization.AwayCover.isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit _ _ _
246	        (fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
247	        (IsLocalization.AwayCover.isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle P.r _ _
248	          (fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
249	          (F.refTriv P)))
250	      (congrArg _ (funext fun i ↦ funext fun j ↦ F.coverCocycle_eq P i j))).trans
251	    (IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_trivializationCocycle P.r _ _
252	      (fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k)))) (F.refTriv P))
253	
254	end transition
255	
256	end TrivializingFamily
257	
258	/-! ## Surjectivity and the dictionary -/
259	
260	namespace CechPic
261	
262	variable (X) [IsAffine X]
263	
264	/-- **Surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism**: every class of invertible
265	modules over the global sections arises from a unit Čech cocycle on a trivializing
266	pointed cover. -/
267	theorem toPic_surjective : Function.Surjective (toPic X) := by
268	  intro c
269	  obtain ⟨F⟩ := TrivializingFamily.nonempty (X := X) (N := c.AsModule)
270	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := PointedCover.BasicRefinement.nonempty F.cover
271	  refine ⟨CechPic.mk F.cover (OneCocycle.class F.cocycle), ?_⟩
272	  rw [toPic_mk F.cover F.cocycle P, F.pic_cocycle P, CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_self]
273	
274	/-- The Čech–Picard descent homomorphism of an affine scheme is an isomorphism. -/
275	theorem toPic_bijective : Function.Bijective (toPic X) :=
276	  ⟨toPic_injective, toPic_surjective X⟩
277	
278	end CechPic
279	
280	/-- **The Čech–Picard dictionary** of an affine scheme: the definitional Čech Picard
281	group on pointed Zariski covers is mathlib's Picard group of invertible modules over
282	the global sections. -/
283	noncomputable def cechPicEquivPic (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
284	    X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤) :=
285	  MulEquiv.ofBijective (CechPic.toPic X) (CechPic.toPic_bijective X)
286	
287	@[simp]
288	lemma cechPicEquivPic_apply (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (c : X.CechPic) :
289	    cechPicEquivPic X c = CechPic.toPic X c :=
290	  rfl
291	
292	end Scheme
293	
294	end AlgebraicGeometry

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FamilyCoboundary

9	/-!
10	# The Čech–Picard dictionary for affine schemes: the descent homomorphism
11	
12	For an affine scheme `X`, this file assembles the Picard classes of unit Čech cocycles
13	along basic refinements (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffineCover`) into an injective
14	group homomorphism
15	
16	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`
17	
18	from the definitional Čech Picard group into mathlib's Picard group of the global
19	sections.  (Surjectivity — hence the full dictionary `X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`
20	— is the invertible-module-trivialization direction, treated separately.)
21	
22	The core is the **independence of the descent Picard class from every choice**
23	(`BasicRefinement.pic_congr`): representing cocycle of the `H¹` class, basic refinement,
24	and pointed cover.  All comparisons are routed through three elementary moves:
25	
26	* `pic_res` — replacing the pointed cover by a finer one and restricting the cocycle
27	  does not change the refinement data nor the class (the restricted evaluations agree on
28	  the nose);
29	* `pic_eq_of_isCohomologous` — cohomologous cocycles give equal classes (the comparison
30	  restricts to an index-wise coboundary; coboundary invariance of the descended module);
31	* `pic_interFst` / `pic_inter` / `pic_interFst_eq_inter` — any two basic refinements of
32	  the same cover are dominated by their merge, on which the two point-selections differ
33	  by the index-wise coboundary of the cross evaluations `γ (pt i, pt' j)`; hence all
34	  refinements give the same class.
35	
36	Injectivity is refinement injectivity: a trivial descent class makes the descent unit a
37	coboundary (`Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_eq_one_iff`), whose components glue back to
38	a coboundary on the pointed cover itself
39	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsH1_eq_one_of_family`).
40	-/

43	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000

57	/-! ## Lifting refinements along cover refinement -/
58	
59	/-- A basic refinement of a finer pointed cover is one of the coarser cover. -/
60	@[simps ι pt r]
61	def ofLE {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (P : 𝒱.BasicRefinement) :
62	    𝒰.BasicRefinement where
63	  ι := P.ι
64	  pt := P.pt
65	  r := P.r
66	  basicOpen_le i := (P.basicOpen_le i).trans (h (P.pt i))
67	  iSup_eq := P.iSup_eq
68	
69	/-- The merge of two basic refinements of the same cover, pointed by the **first**
70	factor.  Defined by updating the points of `inter`, so that the index family and the
71	sections are *definitionally those of `P.inter Q`*. -/
72	@[simps pt]
73	def interFst {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (P Q : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) : 𝒰.BasicRefinement :=
74	  { P.inter Q with
75	    pt := fun p ↦ P.pt p.1
76	    basicOpen_le := fun p ↦
77	      ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_left).trans (P.basicOpen_le p.1) }
78	
79	@[simp]
80	lemma interFst_r {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (P Q : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) (p : P.ι × Q.ι) :
81	    (P.interFst Q).r p = P.r p.1 * Q.r p.2 :=
82	  rfl

88	/-! ## Move 1: restriction along a refinement of pointed covers -/
89	
90	/-- Restricting the cocycle to a finer pointed cover and lifting the basic refinement
91	back does not change the Picard class: the two cover cocycles agree on the nose. -/
92	theorem pic_ofLE (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (P : 𝒱.BasicRefinement) (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
93	    (P.ofLE h).pic γ = P.pic (γ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x)) := by
94	  -- Both sides are `picClass` of `isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit` for the same data:
95	  -- `coverCocycle` of the restricted cocycle is the composed restriction of the same
96	  -- evaluations.
97	  have hcc : (P.ofLE h).coverCocycle γ = P.coverCocycle (γ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x)) := by
98	    funext i j
99	    rw [coverCocycle, coverCocycle, res_unitsEvInf h γ, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
100	    rfl
101	  haveI := (P.ofLE h).faithfullyFlat
102	  haveI := P.faithfullyFlat
103	  exact Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_congr _ _ (congrArg _ hcc)
104	
105	/-! ## Move 2: cohomologous cocycles -/
106	
107	
108	/-- Cohomologous unit cocycles have the same Picard class along any basic refinement. -/
109	theorem pic_eq_of_isCohomologous (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) {γ γ' : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰}
110	    (h : γ.IsCohomologous γ') : P.pic γ = P.pic γ' := by
111	  letI := P.faithfullyFlat
112	  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mp h
113	  -- restate the comparison through the `Γ`-typed interface
114	  have hα' : ∀ z w : X,
115	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens z ⊓ 𝒰.opens w ≤ 𝒰.opens z) (α z)
116	          * unitsEvInf γ z w
117	        = unitsEvInf γ' z w
118	          * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : 𝒰.opens z ⊓ 𝒰.opens w ≤ 𝒰.opens w) (α w) :=
119	    fun z w ↦ hα z w
120	  have hrel : ∀ i j, (P.coverCocycle γ i j).val
121	      = IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclLeft (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
122	          (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
123	          (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i j
124	          ((X.unitsRestrict (P.basicOpen_le i) (α (P.pt i)))⁻¹ : _).val
125	        * ((P.coverCocycle γ' i j).val
126	          * IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclRight (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
127	              (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
128	              (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i j
129	              ((((X.unitsRestrict (P.basicOpen_le j) (α (P.pt j)))⁻¹)⁻¹ : _).val)) := by
130	    intro i j
131	    rw [P.inclLeft_eq_basicRes, P.inclRight_eq_basicRes, inv_inv]
132	    -- units-level form of the component relation
133	    have e := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict (P.overlap_le i j)) (hα' (P.pt i) (P.pt j))
134	    rw [map_mul, map_mul] at e
135	    have key : P.coverCocycle γ i j
136	        = X.unitsRestrict (P.mul_le_left i j)
137	            ((X.unitsRestrict (P.basicOpen_le i) (α (P.pt i)))⁻¹)
138	          * (P.coverCocycle γ' i j
139	            * X.unitsRestrict (P.mul_le_right i j)
140	                ((X.unitsRestrict (P.basicOpen_le j) (α (P.pt j))))) := by
141	      rw [map_inv, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
142	      rw [coverCocycle, coverCocycle]
143	      rw [show X.unitsRestrict ((P.mul_le_left i j).trans (P.basicOpen_le i)) (α (P.pt i))
144	          = X.unitsRestrict (P.overlap_le i j)
145	              (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens (P.pt i) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (P.pt j)
146	                ≤ 𝒰.opens (P.pt i)) (α (P.pt i)))
147	        from (unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict _ _ _).symm,
148	        show X.unitsRestrict ((P.mul_le_right i j).trans (P.basicOpen_le j)) (α (P.pt j))
149	          = X.unitsRestrict (P.overlap_le i j)
150	              (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : 𝒰.opens (P.pt i) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (P.pt j)
151	                ≤ 𝒰.opens (P.pt j)) (α (P.pt j)))
152	        from (unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict _ _ _).symm]
153	      rw [← e]
154	      group
155	    have hval := congrArg Units.val key
156	    simpa only [Units.val_mul, coe_unitsRestrict_basicOpen] using hval
157	  rw [P.pic_eq_picClass γ, P.pic_eq_picClass γ']
158	  exact IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_eq_of_coboundary (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
159	    (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
160	    (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
161	    (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
162	    (P.isCoverCocycle γ') (P.isCoverCocycle γ)
163	    (fun i ↦ (X.unitsRestrict (P.basicOpen_le i) (α (P.pt i)))⁻¹) hrel
164	
165	/-! ## Move 3: change of basic refinement -/
166	
167	/-- Refine-compare along the first projection: the merge pointed by `P` has the same
168	Picard class as `P`. -/
169	theorem pic_interFst (P Q : 𝒰.BasicRefinement)
170	    (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) : (P.interFst Q).pic γ = P.pic γ := by
171	  letI := P.faithfullyFlat
172	  letI := (P.interFst Q).faithfullyFlat
173	  have hτ : ∀ p : P.ι × Q.ι,
174	      IsUnit (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.interFst Q).r p)) (P.r p.1)) :=
175	    fun p ↦ IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd ((P.interFst Q).r p)
176	      (⟨Q.r p.2, rfl⟩ : P.r p.1 ∣ (P.interFst Q).r p)
177	  have hτT : ∀ p q : P.ι × Q.ι,
178	      IsUnit (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤)
179	        Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.interFst Q).r p * (P.interFst Q).r q))
180	        (P.r p.1 * P.r q.1)) :=
181	    fun p q ↦ IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd ((P.interFst Q).r p * (P.interFst Q).r q)
182	      (⟨Q.r p.2 * Q.r q.2, by simp only [interFst_r]; ring⟩ :
183	        P.r p.1 * P.r q.1 ∣ (P.interFst Q).r p * (P.interFst Q).r q)
184	  have hrel : ∀ p q : P.ι × Q.ι, (P.interFst Q).coverCocycle γ p q
185	      = Units.map (IsLocalization.AwayCover.refineOverlapAlgHom (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
186	          (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
187	          (T' := fun p q ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.interFst Q).r p * (P.interFst Q).r q)))
188	          Prod.fst hτT p q).toRingHom.toMonoidHom (P.coverCocycle γ p.1 q.1) := by
189	    intro p q
190	    have hle : X.basicOpen ((P.interFst Q).r p * (P.interFst Q).r q)
191	        ≤ X.basicOpen (P.r p.1 * P.r q.1) :=
192	      X.basicOpen_le_of_dvd ⟨Q.r p.2 * Q.r q.2, by simp only [interFst_r]; ring⟩
193	    have hro : IsLocalization.AwayCover.refineOverlapAlgHom (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
194	          (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
195	          (T' := fun p q ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.interFst Q).r p * (P.interFst Q).r q)))
196	          Prod.fst hτT p q
197	        = X.basicRes _ _ hle :=
198	      X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _
199	    rw [hro]
200	    have hmap : Units.map ((X.basicRes _ _ hle)).toRingHom.toMonoidHom
201	          (P.coverCocycle γ p.1 q.1)
202	        = X.unitsRestrict hle (P.coverCocycle γ p.1 q.1) := rfl
203	    rw [hmap, coverCocycle, coverCocycle, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
204	    rfl
205	  rw [pic_eq_picClass, pic_eq_picClass]
206	  exact IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_map_refine (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
207	    (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
208	    (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
209	    (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
210	    (f' := (P.interFst Q).r)
211	    (S' := fun p ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.interFst Q).r p)))
212	    (T' := fun p q ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.interFst Q).r p * (P.interFst Q).r q)))
213	    Prod.fst hτ hτT
214	    (W' := fun p q t ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.interFst Q).r p
215	      * ((P.interFst Q).r q * (P.interFst Q).r t))))
216	    (P.isCoverCocycle γ) ((P.interFst Q).isCoverCocycle γ) hrel

218	/-- Refine-compare along the second projection: the merge pointed by `Q` has the same
219	Picard class as `Q`. -/
220	theorem pic_inter (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) (Q : 𝒱.BasicRefinement)
221	    (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒱) : (P.inter Q).pic γ = Q.pic γ := by
222	  letI := Q.faithfullyFlat
223	  letI := (P.inter Q).faithfullyFlat
224	  have hτ : ∀ p : P.ι × Q.ι,
225	      IsUnit (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.inter Q).r p)) (Q.r p.2)) :=
226	    fun p ↦ IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd ((P.inter Q).r p)
227	      (⟨P.r p.1, mul_comm _ _⟩ : Q.r p.2 ∣ (P.inter Q).r p)
228	  have hτT : ∀ p q : P.ι × Q.ι,
229	      IsUnit (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤)
230	        Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.inter Q).r p * (P.inter Q).r q))
231	        (Q.r p.2 * Q.r q.2)) :=
232	    fun p q ↦ IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd ((P.inter Q).r p * (P.inter Q).r q)
233	      (⟨P.r p.1 * P.r q.1, by simp only [inter_r]; ring⟩ :
234	        Q.r p.2 * Q.r q.2 ∣ (P.inter Q).r p * (P.inter Q).r q)
235	  have hrel : ∀ p q : P.ι × Q.ι, (P.inter Q).coverCocycle γ p q
236	      = Units.map (IsLocalization.AwayCover.refineOverlapAlgHom (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := Q.r)
237	          (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (Q.r i * Q.r j)))
238	          (T' := fun p q ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.inter Q).r p * (P.inter Q).r q)))
239	          Prod.snd hτT p q).toRingHom.toMonoidHom (Q.coverCocycle γ p.2 q.2) := by
240	    intro p q
241	    have hle : X.basicOpen ((P.inter Q).r p * (P.inter Q).r q)
242	        ≤ X.basicOpen (Q.r p.2 * Q.r q.2) :=
243	      X.basicOpen_le_of_dvd ⟨P.r p.1 * P.r q.1, by simp only [inter_r]; ring⟩
244	    have hro : IsLocalization.AwayCover.refineOverlapAlgHom (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := Q.r)
245	          (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (Q.r i * Q.r j)))
246	          (T' := fun p q ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.inter Q).r p * (P.inter Q).r q)))
247	          Prod.snd hτT p q
248	        = X.basicRes _ _ hle :=
249	      X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _
250	    rw [hro]
251	    have hmap : Units.map ((X.basicRes _ _ hle)).toRingHom.toMonoidHom
252	          (Q.coverCocycle γ p.2 q.2)
253	        = X.unitsRestrict hle (Q.coverCocycle γ p.2 q.2) := rfl
254	    rw [hmap, coverCocycle, coverCocycle, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
255	    rfl
256	  rw [pic_eq_picClass, pic_eq_picClass]
257	  exact IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_map_refine (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := Q.r)
258	    (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (Q.r i)))
259	    (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (Q.r i * Q.r j)))
260	    (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (Q.r i * (Q.r j * Q.r k))))
261	    (f' := (P.inter Q).r)
262	    (S' := fun p ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.inter Q).r p)))
263	    (T' := fun p q ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.inter Q).r p * (P.inter Q).r q)))
264	    Prod.snd hτ hτT
265	    (W' := fun p q t ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen ((P.inter Q).r p
266	      * ((P.inter Q).r q * (P.inter Q).r t))))
267	    (Q.isCoverCocycle γ) ((P.inter Q).isCoverCocycle γ) hrel
